newsitem.title: USA: Lamson says '96 EPS forecasts may be high.
newsitem.headline: Lamson says '96 EPS forecasts may be high.

text.p: Electrical-equipment manufacturer Lamson & Sessions Co Inc said on Thursday pricing pressuring continuing into the fourth quarter is endangering its hopes of meeting Wall Street earnings forecasts for 1996.

"This pricing environment may affect the company's ability to meet analysts' 1996 earnings per share expectations of $1 per share by as much as 10-15 percent," the company said in its third-quarter earnings report.

The company reported third-quarter net income of $4,122,000, or $0.30 a share, an increase of 23 percent from the year-ago quarter. Net sales were $78,098,000, a decrease from $85,716,000 in last year's third quarter of 1995, which included revenues from a unit since sold.

Commenting on the third-quarter results, chief executive John Schulze said, "A difficult pricing environment, combined with rising raw material costs, served to hold down revenues and margins of the electrical conduit and telephone duct portions of our business in the third quarter."
He said growth in large-diamter Vylone pipe and other product lines was strong.
